hint: A generic Node.js HTTP/1.1 client library builds each outgoing request URL by resolving a caller-supplied path (or pathname) against a fixed origin URL. Both the public dispatcher and an internal plain-object URL parser use ordinary relative-URL resolution, which treats a path that begins with two slashes, a backslash-led authority form, a triple slash or an absolute http(s) URL as replacing the authority. An application that passes user input as the path therefore sends the request to a different host and port (SSRF), even though the API contract presents the path as a suffix of the fixed origin. A minimal repair must force the final origin to equal the supplied origin while keeping the supplied text usable as a literal path, and must not break ordinary paths, query-only paths, dot-segment normalization, encoded slashes or same-origin double-slash paths.
surface: Dependency-free Node.js HTTP/1.1 client; public dispatcher accepting an origin plus a path or pathname option; internal URL parser with a plain-object branch and a separate string-path branch; disposable loopback origin and target servers that log request line, Host header and body; library diagnostics channel that exposes the resolved origin and path for each outgoing request.
assumptions: A Node.js runtime is available and the library imports directly from an editable working copy with no installed runtime dependencies.
The observer may read the source, edit two resolution sites in a separate patched copy, and run ordinary HTTP calls.
The attacker controls only the path or pathname string; the application fixes the origin URL and method, and follows no attacker-controlled redirect logic in this scenario.
Disposable HTTP servers can bind ephemeral loopback ports on the loopback interface; one server acts as the fixed origin and a second as the foreign target, and both record every request.
No public target is contacted. The official benchmark verdict is produced externally from an exported patch, so local fixtures and matrices are supporting evidence only.
